To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the first quantum gravitational corrections to the running gauge couplings make all SM gauge interactions asymptoticaly free and assist the three SM gauges to reach unification, irrespective of the logarithmic corrections.
the gravitoninduced universal power-law runnings always assist the three gauge forces to reach asymptotic free unification at the Planck scale.
gravity-assisted asymptotic freedom is realized in the standard model (SM), and the SM Higgs boson is stable up to the Planck scale.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the gauge-invariant power-law runnings of the SM gauge couplings and the SM Higgs mass, induced by quantum gravity.
the gauge-invariant quantum gravity effects in gauge coupling running and Higgs mass bounds.
the quantum corrections to the gauge couplings and Higgs sector from gravity, and the gravity-assisted gauge unification in a gauge invariant way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gravity-assisted gauge unification can occur in the SM with a Higgs boson, and the SM is a viable theory up to the Planck scale.
gravity is not only the weakest but also the most important force in nature.
the gravitational corrections to SM gauge and Higgs sectors can be well described as an effective theory up to energies below 10 16 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gravity is the only known force in nature which can assist the three SM fundamental interactions to unify at the fundamental Planck energy scale.
gravity-assisted gauge unification is a generic feature of the quantum gravity corrections to gauge couplings.
gravity is a necessary ingredient to achieve gauge unification and the Higgs bosons are stable at least up to the Planck scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gravitational corrections to the gauge couplings can be computed reliably and gauge-invariantly, and they always assist gauge unification, and thus the gauge hierarchy problem.
gravity can be treated perturbatively, and the graviton can be integrated out in a gauge-invariant fashion to obtain the first gravitational corrections to gauge couplings.
the graviton-mediated gauge coupling corrections are always universal and positive in the ultraviolet regime, and they are always sufficient to unify the SM gauge couplings.
